skill.name: json-canvas
skill.description: Create and edit JSON Canvas files for Obsidian with valid nodes, edges, groups, links, layout guidance, and validation checks.
skill.summary: Create, update, and validate Obsidian-compatible JSON Canvas files.

content.value_statement: JSON Canvas files are hard to edit by hand without breaking IDs or links. This skill guides creation, updates, and validation for Obsidian-compatible canvases.
actual_capabilities: Create new .canvas structures with nodes, edges, groups, and link nodes.
Add or edit text, file, link, and group nodes with required fields.
Connect nodes with edges, labels, sides, arrow ends, and colors.
Generate 16-character hex IDs and avoid duplicate node or edge IDs.
Validate edge references, node types, colors, and JSON parseability.
Apply layout guidance for spacing, grouping, and grid alignment.
limitations: Does not render or preview Canvas visually by itself.
Does not guarantee compatibility with tools beyond the JSON Canvas specification.
Requires access to the target .canvas file before editing existing canvases.
Does not fetch remote links or verify external URL content.

use_cases.title: Plan a Knowledge Map
use_cases.description: Create a connected canvas that organizes ideas, notes, and relationships for a new topic.

use_cases.title: Build a Project Board
use_cases.description: Generate grouped sections for tasks, status lanes, and dependencies in an Obsidian canvas.

use_cases.title: Organize Research Sources
use_cases.description: Map papers, meeting notes, diagrams, and web references into a connected research workspace.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Canvas
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small visual note.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a JSON Canvas mind map for this topic: [topic]. Include one central idea, three supporting ideas, and clear connecting labels.

prompt_templates.title: Add Nodes to a Canvas
prompt_templates.prompt: Open my existing .canvas file and add these items as new nodes: [items]. Place them without overlap and connect them to related nodes.

prompt_templates.title: Convert an Outline
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn structured notes into a diagram.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this outline into a JSON Canvas layout: [outline]. Use groups for major sections and edges for dependencies or sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Repair and Validate a Canvas
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced cleanup for a complex canvas.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this .canvas file for duplicate IDs, dangling edges, invalid node fields, malformed text strings, and layout collisions. Fix issues and summarize changes.

output_examples.input: Create a mind map for a product launch plan.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a ready-to-save canvas with a central launch node, grouped workstreams, milestone nodes, and labeled dependency edges.

output_examples.input: Add three research sources to my existing canvas.
output_examples.output: The skill adds file and link nodes, places them near the research summary, connects each source, and preserves existing IDs.

output_examples.input: Validate this canvas before I open it in Obsidian.
output_examples.output: The skill reports duplicate IDs, missing target nodes, invalid side values, and unescaped text issues, then proposes corrected entries.

best_practices: Describe the desired layout, node types, and relationships before generating a large canvas.
Validate IDs and edge references after every edit to avoid broken connections.
Use consistent spacing and group bounds so the canvas remains readable in Obsidian.
anti_patterns: Do not paste multiline text without escaping line breaks for JSON strings.
Do not create edges before confirming both node IDs exist.
Do not reuse example IDs when adding multiple nodes or edges.

faq.question: What is JSON Canvas?
faq.answer: JSON Canvas is a file format for visual canvases with nodes and edges. Obsidian uses .canvas files based on this structure.

faq.question: Can this skill edit existing .canvas files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can read an existing canvas, add or change nodes and edges, and keep references valid.

faq.question: Does this skill draw the canvas on screen?
faq.answer: No. It creates and edits the underlying .canvas data that compatible apps can render.

faq.question: Which node types are supported?
faq.answer: It supports text, file, link, and group nodes, including common optional fields for labels, colors, and anchors.

faq.question: How does it prevent broken connections?
faq.answer: It checks that each edge references existing source and target node IDs after creation or editing.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill content is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
